title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
述而不作信而好古
羅星
同考試官教諭鄭批題本平易學者苦為陳言
制縛殊欠灑脫此篇只體夫子語意說去而理明詞
順且不排比為文似當如是
考試官教諭魏批夫子傳道之功正在述而
不作處惟此作能道之
===
考試官教諭林批述作信好字講獨分曉
事惟因於所傳心由切于所仰夫先王所傳皆
心之所仰而不能已焉者也則夫所以因之者
顧無謂哉夫子之意以為道自先王而傳典自
先王而具吾惟懼聖典之或湮也始取而闡明
之大經大法皆因其已具之文恐後世之無傳
也乃收而編次之傳信傳疑悉仍其相沿之舊
刪詩書定禮樂祖述而已矣若别有所制以求
自附于立言之後則吾豈敢乎贊周易脩春秋
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「述而不作，信而好古。」
羅星

同考試官教諭鄭批：題本平易，學者苦為陳言制縛，殊欠灑脫。此篇只體夫子語意說去，而理明詞順，且不排比，為文似當如是。
考試官教諭魏批：夫子傳道之功，正在述而不作處，惟此作能道之。
考試官教諭林批：述、作、信、好字，講獨分曉。

事惟因於所傳，心由切于所仰。夫先王所傳，皆心之所仰而不能已焉者也，則夫所以因之者，顧無謂哉？夫子之意以為：道自先王而傳，典自先王而具。吾惟懼聖典之或湮也，始取而闡明之，大經大法，皆因其已具之文；恐後世之無傳也，乃收而編次之，傳信傳疑，悉仍其相沿之舊。刪詩書，定禮樂，祖述而已矣。若别有所制，以求自附于立言之後，則吾豈敢乎？贊周易，脩春秋，
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“I transmit but do not create; I trust in and love antiquity.”
Luo Xing

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: The topic is straightforward, but students are painfully constrained by stock expressions and show a marked lack of ease and freedom. This essay simply follows the meaning of the Master's words as it develops its argument. Its reasoning is clear and its language flows smoothly; moreover, it does not arrange its phrases in parallel series. This seems to be how an essay ought to be written.

Comment by Examiner Wei, Instructor: The Master's achievement in transmitting the Way lies precisely in his transmitting without creating. This essay alone succeeds in expressing it.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Its explanation of the words “transmit,” “create,” “trust,” and “love” is exceptionally clear.

In his undertakings, he followed what had been handed down; in his heart, he was deeply attached to what he revered. What the former kings transmitted was all that his heart revered and could not cease to cherish. Could his following it, then, have been without purpose? The Master's meaning was this: The Way has been transmitted from the former kings, and the canonical writings were fully established by them. Fearing only that the sages' canonical writings might fall into oblivion, I took them up and elucidated them. In their great principles and great rules, I followed throughout the texts already in existence. Fearing that later generations would have nothing handed down to them, I gathered these writings and arranged them in order. In transmitting what was certain as certain and what was doubtful as doubtful, I adhered throughout to the inherited practice. In editing the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, and establishing rites and music, I merely followed and transmitted what had come before. As for devising something separately, seeking thereby to join the ranks of those who established enduring teachings, how would I dare? In elucidating the Changes of Zhou and compiling the Spring and Autumn Annals, …

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
傳述而已矣若更有所作以求欲相侔於開物之
功豈我所能乎所以然者以我亦惟信古而好之焉
耳盖古焉弗信或疑之而妄有所作吾則信之
也篤而知其言之不誣信焉弗好又忽之而漫
無所述我則好之也專而味其意之無倦言必
詩書用惟禮樂想像之頃恍若精神之與合雖
欲不傳情能以自已耶心存周易志在春秋孚
契之餘儼乎形容之若見雖欲立異心能以自
安耶吁作固夫子之能事也乃辭之而以述自
===
居其謙己之意至矣抑夫子賢於堯舜者也而
於作焉猶爾今既不敢當作者之聖而於老彭
之賢亦不敢顯然以自附盖盛德之言有如此
者然集群聖之大成而折衷之其事雖述而功
則倍於作矣噫以此垂訓後世猶有續經擬經
以自僭者何哉
凡事豫則立不豫則廢言前定則不跲事
前定則不困行前定則不疚道前定則不
窮
punctuated:
傳述而已矣。若更有所作，以求欲相侔於開物之功，豈我所能乎？所以然者，以我亦惟信古而好之焉耳。盖古焉弗信，或疑之而妄有所作，吾則信之也篤，而知其言之不誣；信焉弗好，又忽之而漫無所述，我則好之也專，而味其意之無倦。言必詩書，用惟禮樂，想像之頃，恍若精神之與合，雖欲不傳，情能以自已耶？心存周易，志在春秋，孚契之餘，儼乎形容之若見，雖欲立異，心能以自安耶？吁！作固夫子之能事也，乃辭之而以述自居，其謙己之意至矣。抑夫子賢於堯舜者也，而於作焉猶爾。今既不敢當作者之聖，而於老彭之賢，亦不敢顯然以自附，盖盛德之言有如此者。然集群聖之大成而折衷之，其事雖述，而功則倍於作矣。噫！以此垂訓後世，猶有續經擬經以自僭者，何哉？

凡事豫則立，不豫則廢。言前定則不跲，事前定則不困，行前定則不疚，道前定則不窮。
translation_en:
…merely transmitting and recounting. “Were I further to create something, seeking thereby to equal the achievement of opening up an understanding of things, how could that be within my powers? The reason is simply that I trust antiquity and delight in it. If one does not trust antiquity, one may doubt it and rashly create something of one’s own. My trust, however, is firm, and I know that its words are not false. If one trusts it but does not delight in it, one may neglect it and carelessly fail to transmit anything. My delight, however, is wholehearted, and I savor its meaning without weariness. My speech invariably draws upon the Odes and Documents; my practice follows only ritual and music. As I picture antiquity, it seems that my spirit joins with that of the ancients. Even if I wished not to transmit their legacy, could my feelings allow me to stop? My heart rests in the Changes of Zhou, and my aspirations lie in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Through this trusting accord, it is as though I could distinctly see the ancients’ very forms. Even if I wished to establish something different, could my heart be at ease?”

Ah! Creating was certainly within the Master’s powers, yet he disclaimed it and placed himself among transmitters. His intention to humble himself was utmost indeed. Moreover, the Master surpassed Yao and Shun in worth, yet even toward creating he took this attitude. Here, not only did he dare not claim the sagehood of a creator; he did not even dare openly to rank himself with the worthy Lao Peng. Such are the words of one whose virtue is abundant. Yet he brought together the great accomplishments of all the sages and established a balanced standard among them. Although his work was transmission, his achievement was twice that of creation. Alas! With such instruction handed down to later generations, why are there still those who presumptuously continue the Classics or compose imitations of them?

In all matters, preparation brings success; without preparation, they fail. When words are settled beforehand, one does not stumble in speech. When affairs are settled beforehand, one does not encounter difficulty. When conduct is settled beforehand, one has no cause for regret. When one’s course is settled beforehand, one does not reach an impasse.

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
丁濬
同考試官教諭李批於豫於前定處見誠極難
下筆摹寫似此其邃於體認者歟
考試官教諭魏批跲困疚窮之義作者多失
之晦此獨能發揮得出錄之
考試官教諭林批如此作要亦思致之精到
者
中庸論事當先立乎誠而必推誠之所以當先
立也蓋誠爲萬事之本誠豫而事立自然之理
===
耳中庸得不推言其意哉昔孔子告哀公問政
及此謂夫人君以達德而行達道以九經而爲
天下國家皆本於誠也誠豈襲取之可得哉養
之於念慮未動之先而心體素明存之於事物
未來之際而操持素定則道可由也德可據也
而九經莫非實事矣凡事有不立哉其或雜於
私僞而無純一專確之念趨於苟簡而無真積
力久之功則道相離也德相悖也而九經莫非
虛文矣凡事有不廢哉事之立與廢係於誠之
punctuated:
丁濬。

同考試官教諭李批：於豫、於前定處見誠，極難下筆摹寫。似此，其邃於體認者歟！

考試官教諭魏批：跲、困、疚、窮之義，作者多失之晦，此獨能發揮得出，錄之。

考試官教諭林批：如此作，要亦思致之精到者。

中庸論事當先立乎誠，而必推誠之所以當先立也。蓋誠爲萬事之本，誠豫而事立，自然之理耳。中庸得不推言其意哉？昔孔子告哀公問政，及此，謂夫人君以達德而行達道，以九經而爲天下國家，皆本於誠也。誠豈襲取之可得哉？養之於念慮未動之先，而心體素明；存之於事物未來之際，而操持素定，則道可由也，德可據也，而九經莫非實事矣。凡事有不立哉？其或雜於私僞，而無純一專確之念；趨於苟簡，而無真積力久之功，則道相離也，德相悖也，而九經莫非虛文矣。凡事有不廢哉？事之立與廢，係於誠之
translation_en:
Ding Jun.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: To discern sincerity in “preparation” and “determination beforehand” is exceedingly difficult to capture in writing. Surely someone who writes like this has attained a profound personal understanding!

Comment by Examiner Wei, Instructor: Writers often leave the meanings of stumbling, difficulty, remorse, and exhaustion obscure. This writer alone brings them fully to light. Include this answer.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Writing like this surely also shows precision and depth of thought.

In discussing affairs, the Doctrine of the Mean holds that sincerity must first be established, and necessarily explores why it must be established first. Sincerity is the foundation of all affairs: when sincerity is prepared beforehand, affairs succeed. This is simply the natural principle. How could the Doctrine of the Mean fail to expound its meaning? Long ago, when Confucius answered Duke Ai’s questions about government, he touched upon this point, saying that a ruler’s practice of the universally applicable Way through the universally applicable virtues, and his governance of the realm, state, and family through the nine guiding principles, are all rooted in sincerity. How could sincerity be obtained by seizing it from outside? Nurture it before thoughts begin to stir, so that the heart’s essential substance is already clear; preserve it before affairs and things present themselves, so that one’s self-command is already settled. Then the Way can be followed and virtue relied upon, and every one of the nine guiding principles becomes a substantive practice. Could any undertaking fail to succeed? If, however, selfishness and falsity intrude, leaving no purity, unity, concentration, and firmness of purpose, and one inclines toward careless expediency, without the achievement of genuine accumulation and sustained effort, then one departs from the Way and runs counter to virtue, and all nine guiding principles become empty formalities. Could any undertaking fail to collapse? The success or failure of affairs depends upon sincerity’s …

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
豫與不豫如此烏可以誠爲後而不前定乎是
故唯諾應對之未形而誠已具言前定矣隨其
所語有上下而淺深詳畧之節井如也何跲之
有酬酢施爲之未著而誠已存事前定矣隨其
所處有常變而錯綜斟酌之𥙿如也何困之
有措於躬者或未免慙于志行不豫也前定乎
誠則所見真切而行有常發邇見遠隨寓而無
不慊矣夫何疚足於此者或不能通於彼道不
豫也前定乎誠則所資深遠而道有本千變萬
===
化隨取而無不足矣夫何窮惟至誠爲能定惟
誠定爲能立反是則不豫而皆廢矣中庸引此
以明道之費隱有以夫大抵天下國家之本在
於身身之本在於心心之要在於誠一誠之立
萬化之源也其所繫不亦重乎孔子推明素定
之理以爲哀公告下文又詳言學問之功而示
以入誠之方其所以啓之者可謂明且切矣而
哀公蔽固已深終不能繹孔子之言舉文武之
政一變而至於道也惜哉
punctuated: 豫與不豫如此，烏可以誠爲後而不前定乎？是故唯諾應對之未形，而誠已具，言前定矣。隨其所語有上下，而淺深詳畧之節井如也，何跲之有？酬酢施爲之未著，而誠已存，事前定矣。隨其所處有常變，而錯綜斟酌之𥙿如也，何困之有？措於躬者或未免慙于志，行不豫也。前定乎誠，則所見真切而行有常，發邇見遠，隨寓而無不慊矣，夫何疚？足於此者或不能通於彼，道不豫也。前定乎誠，則所資深遠而道有本，千變萬化，隨取而無不足矣，夫何窮？惟至誠爲能定，惟誠定爲能立，反是則不豫而皆廢矣。《中庸》引此以明道之費隱，有以夫！大抵天下國家之本在於身，身之本在於心，心之要在於誠。一誠之立，萬化之源也，其所繫不亦重乎？孔子推明素定之理，以爲哀公告，下文又詳言學問之功，而示以入誠之方，其所以啓之者可謂明且切矣。而哀公蔽固已深，終不能繹孔子之言，舉文武之政，一變而至於道也。惜哉！
translation_en:
…whether sincerity is prepared beforehand or not makes such a difference. How, then, could one put sincerity last and fail to establish it in advance? Thus, before words of assent and reply have taken shape, sincerity is already complete: speech has been settled beforehand. Whether one speaks to superiors or inferiors, the proper degrees of depth and simplicity, detail and brevity are well ordered. What stumbling in speech could there be? Before dealings with others and practical undertakings become manifest, sincerity is already present: affairs have been settled beforehand. Whether the circumstances encountered are ordinary or exceptional, one has ample capacity to coordinate and weigh them. What difficulty could there be? If what one puts into practice still leaves one ashamed before one’s own intentions, this is because conduct has not been prepared beforehand. If it is settled beforehand through sincerity, one’s understanding is true and keen, and one’s conduct constant. Beginning with what is near, it manifests itself far away; wherever one finds oneself, there is nothing that fails to satisfy the conscience. What remorse could there be? If what suffices here cannot be applied there, this is because the Way has not been prepared beforehand. If it is settled beforehand through sincerity, the resources on which one draws are deep and far-reaching, and the Way has a foundation. Through a thousand changes and ten thousand transformations, wherever one draws upon it, it never proves insufficient. How could it ever be exhausted? Only utmost sincerity can bring settled resolve; only when sincerity is settled can things be established. Conversely, without preparation, everything falls into ruin. The Doctrine of the Mean quotes this to illuminate the Way’s expansive operation and hidden subtlety, and with good reason!

In general, the foundation of all under Heaven, the state, and the family lies in the person; the foundation of the person lies in the mind; and the essential requirement of the mind lies in sincerity. The establishment of sincerity alone is the source of all transformation. Is not what depends upon it of the greatest consequence? Kongzi elucidated the principle of being settled beforehand in order to instruct Duke Ai. In the following passage, he further explained in detail the work of study and inquiry, showing him the means of entering into sincerity. His guidance may indeed be called clear and pointed. Yet Duke Ai’s blindness and obstinacy were already deep. In the end, he could not draw out the meaning of Kongzi’s words and put into effect the government of Kings Wen and Wu, thereby attaining the Way through a single transformation. What a pity!

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
有布縷之征粟米之征力役之征君子用
其一緩其二
羅雲
同考試官教諭吳批此題上三句是定賦下乃
說取之之法朱子註意甚明場中作者率顛倒冗俗
詞意足以發之而鋪叙明整僅見此耳
同考試官教諭陳批一歲之賦三時取之先王
之法能提掇明白如此者不多見也
同考試官學正周批不作綺麗語只平平遺去
===
而孟子當時論賦意思却明悉
考試官教諭魏批三股文字筆力似此者亦
難得
考試官教諭林批錄此取其潔也
大賢論賦定於一歲者而不併取於一時也夫
歲有常賦取之當各以其時也苟併用之而無
節焉則民有不堪者矣君子豈為之哉孟子因
當時諸侯取民無度而警之以此蓋謂為國不
能不取於民而亦不可併取於民是故布縷之
punctuated:
有布縷之征、粟米之征、力役之征，君子用其一，緩其二。
羅雲
同考試官教諭吳批：此題上三句是定賦，下乃說取之之法，朱子註意甚明。場中作者率顛倒冗俗，詞意足以發之，而鋪叙明整，僅見此耳。
同考試官教諭陳批：一歲之賦，三時取之，先王之法。能提掇明白如此者，不多見也。
同考試官學正周批：不作綺麗語，只平平遺去，而孟子當時論賦意思却明悉。
考試官教諭魏批：三股文字，筆力似此者，亦難得。
考試官教諭林批：錄此，取其潔也。
大賢論賦，定於一歲者，而不併取於一時也。夫歲有常賦，取之當各以其時也。苟併用之而無節焉，則民有不堪者矣，君子豈為之哉？孟子因當時諸侯取民無度，而警之以此。蓋謂為國不能不取於民，而亦不可併取於民。是故布縷之
translation_en:
“There are levies of cloth and thread, levies of grain, and levies of labor service. The gentleman employs one and defers the other two.”

Luo Yun

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: The first three clauses of this topic specify the established taxes; what follows explains how to collect them. Master Zhu’s meaning in his commentary is very clear. Most candidates in the examination hall have reversed this relationship and written prolix, commonplace prose. This is the only piece I have seen whose wording and ideas adequately elucidate the topic and whose exposition is clear and orderly.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Collecting the taxes for one year at three different seasons was the method of the former kings. Few essays bring out the essentials as clearly as this one.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, School Instructor: He does not compose ornate phrases, but simply proceeds in a plain manner [?]; nevertheless, Mencius’s meaning in discussing taxation at that time is made fully clear.

Comment by Examiner Wei, Instructor: Among essays in three sections, writing of such strength is also hard to find.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: I select this piece for inclusion on account of its clean prose.

The great worthy discusses taxes fixed for the year, which are not to be collected all at once. Each year has its regular taxes, and each should be collected at its proper season. If all are exacted together without restraint, the people will find the burden unbearable. How could the gentleman do such a thing? Because the feudal lords of his time exacted taxes from the people without measure, Mencius warned them with these words. His meaning was that governing a state necessarily entails taking from the people, yet one must not take everything from them at once. Thus, as for cloth and thread …

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
需經費有必資焉者則因民之有蠶績也而為
之賦之繭焉以獻績焉以供而布縷之征於是
乎行焉粟米之用儲蓄有必賴焉者則因民之
有稼穡也而為之賦之都鄙以貢鄉遂以助而
粟米之征於是乎興焉凡有興作民之力役又
在所當籍矣則因民之力而賦之壯者於其力
工者於其能力役之征又不于此而定哉夫賦
民之法歲有常數如此君子以為蠶績乃成布
縷其時也故於夏而用之者亦惟布縷而已矣
===
外此而粟米而力役則必緩之不併取以重民
之困也稼穡乃登粟米其時也故於秋而用之
者亦惟粟米而已矣外此而力役而布縷則又
緩之不兼用以竭民之財也歲晚務閑民力可
用茲又其時矣故力役用之於冬一有興作取
能于其工也取力于其壯也而布縷粟米之征
則徐待其時焉其忍取盈于畝以傷民之心乎
是則雖取于民而民不加損先王之經制固如
是哉大抵民者邦之本也本固邦寧財者民之
punctuated: 需，經費有必資焉者，則因民之有蠶績也而為之賦之，繭焉以獻，績焉以供，而布縷之征於是乎行焉。粟米之用，儲蓄有必賴焉者，則因民之有稼穡也而為之賦之，都鄙以貢，鄉遂以助，而粟米之征於是乎興焉。凡有興作，民之力役又在所當籍矣，則因民之力而賦之，壯者於其力，工者於其能，力役之征又不于此而定哉？夫賦民之法，歲有常數如此。君子以為蠶績乃成，布縷其時也，故於夏而用之者亦惟布縷而已矣。外此而粟米而力役，則必緩之，不併取以重民之困也。稼穡乃登，粟米其時也，故於秋而用之者亦惟粟米而已矣。外此而力役而布縷，則又緩之，不兼用以竭民之財也。歲晚務閑，民力可用，茲又其時矣。故力役用之於冬，一有興作，取能于其工也，取力于其壯也，而布縷粟米之征則徐待其時焉。其忍取盈于畝以傷民之心乎？是則雖取于民，而民不加損，先王之經制固如是哉！大抵民者邦之本也，本固邦寧；財者民之
translation_en: …requirements for cloth and thread are indispensable to regular expenditure. Accordingly, the people are assessed on their sericulture and spinning: cocoons are presented and spun thread supplied. Thus the levy of cloth and thread is put into effect. Grain is indispensable for building up reserves. Accordingly, the people are assessed on their cultivation and harvesting: the capital and outlying domains furnish tribute, while the inner and outer rural districts provide assistance. Thus the grain levy is instituted. Whenever construction projects arise, the people's labor must also be requisitioned. They are therefore assessed according to their capacity: the able-bodied contribute their strength, and artisans their skills. Is this not also how the labor levy is determined? Such are the fixed annual assessments prescribed for taxing the people. The gentleman considers that when sericulture and spinning are completed, the season for cloth and thread has arrived. Thus, in summer, he imposes only the levy of cloth and thread. The other levies, of grain and labor, must be deferred; they are not exacted together, lest the people's hardship be increased. When the crops have been harvested, the season for grain has arrived. Thus, in autumn, he imposes only the grain levy. The other levies, of labor and cloth and thread, are again deferred; they are not imposed together, lest the people's resources be exhausted. Late in the year, when agricultural tasks are slack and the people's labor is available, the appropriate season for this levy has likewise arrived. Thus labor is requisitioned in winter. Whenever construction projects arise, artisans contribute their skills and the able-bodied their strength, while the levies of cloth and thread and grain await their respective seasons. How could he bear to exact the full amount from the fields and thereby wound the people's hearts? In this way, although resources are taken from the people, they suffer no additional loss. Such indeed were the established institutions of the former kings! In general, the people are the foundation of the state: when the foundation is firm, the state is at peace. Wealth is the people's…

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
心也財聚民散君子之所以以義爲利者正欲
民之有餘而已國之不足非所患也昔人謂百
姓足君孰與不足知本之論槩如此世之不知
撫民而用二甚至於用三焉古法至此蕩然無
復存者噫民殍且離國豈能以獨富乎其亦不
思之甚矣
易
大哉乾元萬物資始乃統天
羅星
===
同考試官教諭鄭批說出資始乃統天處一氣
流行甚明場中類以四德並講殊戾元義不見聖人
嘆元之所以為大取而錄之例其餘也
考試官教諭魏批得彖傳釋乾元之旨
考試官教諭林批辭贍意足
彖傳贊乾元之大肇庶類而專化育焉甚矣庶
類至繁而化育之功尤盡也乾元有以肇其始
而專其功焉可以見其大矣昔伏羲畫卦以乾
為首文王繫辭以元爲端蓋乾乃天之性情而
punctuated:
心也。財聚民散，君子之所以以義爲利者，正欲民之有餘而已，國之不足非所患也。昔人謂：「百姓足，君孰與不足？」知本之論槩如此。世之不知撫民而用二，甚至於用三焉，古法至此蕩然無復存者。噫！民殍且離，國豈能以獨富乎？其亦不思之甚矣！

易
大哉乾元，萬物資始，乃統天。
羅星

同考試官教諭鄭批：說出資始乃統天處，一氣流行甚明。場中類以四德並講，殊戾元義，不見聖人嘆元之所以為大。取而錄之，例其餘也。
考試官教諭魏批：得彖傳釋乾元之旨。
考試官教諭林批：辭贍意足。

彖傳贊乾元之大，肇庶類而專化育焉。甚矣，庶類至繁，而化育之功尤盡也！乾元有以肇其始而專其功焉，可以見其大矣。昔伏羲畫卦，以乾為首；文王繫辭，以元爲端。蓋乾乃天之性情，而
translation_en:
…heart. When wealth accumulates, the people scatter. The gentleman therefore regards righteousness as profit precisely because he wishes the people to have more than enough; insufficiency in the state’s resources is not his concern. Someone of old said: “If the common people have enough, how could their ruler alone lack enough?” Such, in general, is an argument that understands the foundation. Those in this age who do not know how to care for the people impose two levies at once, or even all three. At this point the ancient institutions have been utterly swept away, with nothing remaining. Alas! When the people starve to death and disperse, how can the state alone remain wealthy? This is thoughtlessness indeed!

Book of Changes
“Great indeed is the primal power of Qian! All things depend upon it for their beginning; thus it comprehends Heaven.”
Luo Xing

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The essay explains how ‘all things depend upon it for their beginning’ leads to ‘thus it comprehends Heaven,’ making the circulation of a single vital force very clear. Candidates in this examination generally discuss all four virtues together, seriously departing from the meaning of the primal and failing to show why the sage extols its greatness. We select and record this essay as a standard for the others.”
Comment by Examiner Wei, Instructor: “It grasps the purport of the Commentary on the Judgments in explaining the primal power of Qian.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Rich in expression and full in meaning.”

The Commentary on the Judgments praises the greatness of Qian’s primal power: it initiates the myriad kinds of beings and has sole command of their transformation and nurture. How extraordinary! The kinds of beings are exceedingly numerous, yet the work of transforming and nurturing them is all the more complete. Qian’s primal power initiates their beginnings and has sole command of this work; herein its greatness may be seen. In antiquity, when Fu Xi drew the hexagrams, he placed Qian first; when King Wen appended the statements, he began with the primal. For Qian is Heaven’s nature and disposition, and…

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
元其德之大始也孔子傳彖而賛之曰大哉乾
之元乎何以見之蓋當夫肅殺之餘生意或幾
乎泯矣氣一動焉而物即與之俱動凝寂之時
化機或幾乎息矣帝一出焉而物即與之俱出
洪纖高下類雖不一也咸藉是以爲之端倪動
植飛潜數極于萬也皆資焉以爲之朕兆斡自
靜而動之機造自无而有之化蓋无一物而能
外焉其施可謂博矣然乃肇造於始而自達其
流行之機發露於初而馴致夫變化之道由是
===
而流形而正命人皆曰亨利之功也而不知推
行於兩間者皆是氣之貫徹由是而正命而歸
根人皆曰利貞之德也而不知順布於四時者
皆是理之充周妙乾行之不息引化育於无窮
蓋无一時而或間焉其功可謂專矣乾元之大
不於是而見乎抑天道之元賦於人爲仁故仁
兼萬善統四端猶元之始萬物而統四時也是
以天體元而美利天下聖人體仁則萬國咸寧
蓋天體物不遺而仁體事无不在也學者求至
punctuated: 元，其德之大始也。孔子傳彖而賛之曰：「大哉，乾之元乎！」何以見之？蓋當夫肅殺之餘，生意或幾乎泯矣，氣一動焉，而物即與之俱動；凝寂之時，化機或幾乎息矣，帝一出焉，而物即與之俱出。洪纖高下，類雖不一也，咸藉是以爲之端倪；動植飛潜，數極于萬也，皆資焉以爲之朕兆。斡自靜而動之機，造自无而有之化，蓋无一物而能外焉，其施可謂博矣。然乃肇造於始，而自達其流行之機；發露於初，而馴致夫變化之道。由是而流形而正命，人皆曰亨利之功也，而不知推行於兩間者，皆是氣之貫徹；由是而正命而歸根，人皆曰利貞之德也，而不知順布於四時者，皆是理之充周。妙乾行之不息，引化育於无窮，蓋无一時而或間焉，其功可謂專矣。乾元之大，不於是而見乎？抑天道之元，賦於人爲仁，故仁兼萬善，統四端，猶元之始萬物而統四時也。是以天體元而美利天下，聖人體仁則萬國咸寧。蓋天體物不遺，而仁體事无不在也。學者求至
translation_en:
…and yuan, origination, is the great beginning of its virtue. Confucius, commenting on the hexagram judgment, praised it, saying: “Great indeed is the originating power of Qian!” How is this evident? After the season of chilling destruction, the impulse of life may seem almost extinguished; yet once vital energy stirs, things immediately stir together with it. In the season of frozen stillness, the workings of transformation may seem almost to have ceased; yet once the Lord comes forth, things immediately come forth together with him. Great and small, high and low, though their kinds differ, all depend on this for their beginnings. Moving and rooted, flying and submerged, though they number in the myriad, all draw upon it for their first signs of emergence. It turns the mechanism that leads from stillness to movement and brings about the transformation from nonbeing to being. Nothing can stand outside it: its beneficence may indeed be called all-embracing. Yet, having initiated creation at the beginning, it itself carries through the workings of its circulation; having manifested itself at the outset, it gradually brings the course of change and transformation to completion.
Through this, things assume their forms and attain their proper allotted natures. Everyone calls this the achievement of heng and li—free development and benefit—without knowing that what operates between Heaven and Earth is this same vital energy penetrating throughout. Through this, things attain their proper allotted natures and return to their roots. Everyone calls this the virtue of li and zhen—benefit and constancy—without knowing that what spreads in due order through the four seasons is this same principle filling all things. Wondrously sustaining Qian’s unceasing movement, it extends transformation and nurture without limit. There is never a moment of interruption: its achievement may indeed be called sovereign. Is not the greatness of Qian’s originating power evident in this?
Moreover, the originating power of the Way of Heaven, when endowed in human beings, becomes benevolence. Thus benevolence embraces all goodness and unites the four moral beginnings, just as origination gives beginning to the myriad things and governs the four seasons. Hence Heaven embodies origination and brings excellent benefits to all under Heaven; when the sage embodies benevolence, the myriad states are all at peace. Heaven gives substance to things without omitting any, while benevolence gives substance to affairs and is present everywhere. Learners who seek to attain…

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
於聖人亦曰自強不息以體夫天行之健□
如是則文王所謂元亨利貞者其蘊乃盡而孔
子之易未必非文王之易也
易簡而天下之理得矣天下之理得而成
位乎其中矣
程轍
同考試官教諭鄭批理本自然凡有所艱難煩
擾則是未離於欲而理猶為二耳易簡則無所容心
故理無不得場中多以一本而貫萬殊為說甚悖乾
===
知坤能之義子獨能發明其說必其究心易學久矣
考試官教諭魏批發揮明透刻之
考試官教諭林批說聖人與天地合德處最是
惟兼體乎乾坤之道則可以配天地矣夫乾坤
之道易簡而已人既有以兼體其道而又何忝
哉大傳因明作經之理而言人當盡體道之功
至此謂夫乾坤之理具於易書學易者豈惟以
成賢人之德業哉是故志氣精純而有獨運之
力日用之間當行即行而不為人欲之沮撓一
punctuated:
於聖人，亦曰自強不息，以體夫天行之健□。如是，則文王所謂元亨利貞者，其蘊乃盡，而孔子之易未必非文王之易也。

易簡而天下之理得矣，天下之理得而成位乎其中矣。

程轍

同考試官教諭鄭批：理本自然，凡有所艱難煩擾，則是未離於欲，而理猶為二耳。易簡則無所容心，故理無不得。場中多以一本而貫萬殊為說，甚悖乾知坤能之義。子獨能發明其說，必其究心易學久矣。

考試官教諭魏批：發揮明透，刻之。

考試官教諭林批：說聖人與天地合德處最是。

惟兼體乎乾坤之道，則可以配天地矣。夫乾坤之道，易簡而已。人既有以兼體其道，而又何忝哉？大傳因明作經之理，而言人當盡體道之功。至此，謂夫乾坤之理具於易書，學易者豈惟以成賢人之德業哉？是故志氣精純，而有獨運之力，日用之間，當行即行，而不為人欲之沮撓，一…
translation_en:
…to attain sagehood, one need only strive unceasingly to embody the vigor of Heaven’s movement [illegible character]. Thus the full significance of what King Wen called “the originating, the penetrating, the beneficial, and the steadfast” is exhausted, and Confucius’s Changes need not be different from King Wen’s Changes.

“Through ease and simplicity, the principles of all under Heaven are grasped. When the principles of all under Heaven are grasped, one establishes one’s position in their midst.”

Cheng Zhe 程轍

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Principle is inherently natural. Wherever there is difficulty or vexatious disturbance, one has not yet freed oneself from desire, and principle remains something separate. With ease and simplicity, there is no room for deliberate contrivance; hence no principle remains ungrasped. Many candidates in this examination have explained this in terms of a single root running through the myriad particulars. This seriously contradicts the meaning of Qian’s knowing and Kun’s capacity. You alone have elucidated this teaching; surely you have long devoted yourself to studying the Changes.

Comment by Examiner Wei, Instructor: The exposition is lucid and penetrating. Have it printed.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: The passage explaining how the sage accords in virtue with Heaven and Earth is particularly sound.

Only by embodying together the ways of Qian and Kun can one stand as a counterpart to Heaven and Earth. The ways of Qian and Kun are simply ease and simplicity. Once a person can embody both their ways, how could he fall short? In explaining the principles underlying the composition of the classic, the Great Commentary says that people should fully accomplish the work of embodying the Way. At this point, it means that the principles of Qian and Kun are fully contained in the Book of Changes. Can those who study the Changes be seeking merely to perfect the virtue and achievements of a worthy person? Thus, when one’s resolve and vital energy are refined and pure, possessing the power to act independently, one acts in daily life whenever action is called for, without being obstructed by human desires, wholly …

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
乾之以易而知始焉方寸靜虛而極感孚之□□
應酬之際隨物付物而无事私智之造作一坤
之以簡而成物焉則理在萬殊本不外乎身也
而撓於私欲斯失之耳今焉當行即行而不見
其難則无行而不適其宜夫焉有不獲乎理寓
萬物本皆備於我也而役於私智斯失之耳今
焉隨物付物而不見其煩則无物而不得其當
又焉有不獲乎吾知天之所以為天者以易而
知天下之物也吾亦以易而得天下之理天何
===
所加於我哉地之所以為地者以簡而成天下
之物也吾亦以簡而得天下之理吾何所歉於
地哉天位乎上其大无加焉耳人身雖眇而德
則有以配其无垠夫何異地位乎下其廣無加
焉耳人身雖微而德則有以應其无疆夫何殊
是豈不有以成位其中而參為三才也歟至此
則體道之極功聖人之能事而不徒為賢人之
德業矣大抵天下同歸而殊途一致而百慮故
□□者失道而易簡則理得矣天地與人本同
punctuated: 乾之以易而知始焉。方寸靜虛，而極感孚之□□；應酬之際，隨物付物，而无事私智之造作，一坤之以簡而成物焉。則理在萬殊，本不外乎身也，而撓於私欲，斯失之耳。今焉當行即行，而不見其難，則无行而不適其宜，夫焉有不獲乎？理寓萬物，本皆備於我也，而役於私智，斯失之耳。今焉隨物付物，而不見其煩，則无物而不得其當，又焉有不獲乎？吾知天之所以為天者，以易而知天下之物也；吾亦以易而得天下之理，天何所加於我哉？地之所以為地者，以簡而成天下之物也；吾亦以簡而得天下之理，吾何所歉於地哉？天位乎上，其大无加焉耳；人身雖眇，而德則有以配其无垠，夫何異？地位乎下，其廣無加焉耳；人身雖微，而德則有以應其无疆，夫何殊？是豈不有以成位其中，而參為三才也歟？至此，則體道之極功，聖人之能事，而不徒為賢人之德業矣。大抵天下同歸而殊途，一致而百慮，故□□者失道，而易簡則理得矣。天地與人本同
translation_en:
…like Qian, knowing beginnings through ease. The heart is still and empty, bringing responsive sincerity to its utmost [?; two illegible characters]. In responding to affairs, one deals with each thing according to its own nature, without contrivances of private cleverness, wholly like Kun, bringing things to completion through simplicity. Principle exists amid countless differences, yet fundamentally lies nowhere outside oneself; it is only when disturbed by selfish desires that one loses it. Now, if one acts whenever action is called for and finds no difficulty in doing so, every action will accord with what is fitting. How, then, could one fail to attain it? Principle inheres in the myriad things, yet is originally fully present within oneself; it is only when enslaved by private cleverness that one loses it. Now, if one deals with each thing according to its own nature and finds no vexation in doing so, every thing will receive its proper treatment. How, again, could one fail to attain it?

I know that what makes Heaven Heaven is its knowing the things of the world through ease. If I too attain the principles of the world through ease, in what way does Heaven surpass me? What makes Earth Earth is its bringing the things of the world to completion through simplicity. If I too attain the principles of the world through simplicity, in what way do I fall short of Earth? Heaven occupies its place above, and nothing exceeds its greatness. Though the human body is tiny, its virtue can match Heaven’s boundlessness: what difference, then, is there? Earth occupies its place below, and nothing exceeds its breadth. Though the human body is minute, its virtue can correspond to Earth’s limitless extent: what distinction, then, is there? Does this not enable humans to establish their place between Heaven and Earth and join them as the Three Powers? At this point, one reaches the highest achievement in embodying the Way, the accomplishment of the sage, and no longer merely the virtue and undertakings of the worthy.

Generally speaking, all under Heaven reaches the same destination by different paths and arrives at one outcome through a hundred deliberations. Thus, those who [two illegible characters] lose the Way, whereas through ease and simplicity principle is attained. Heaven, Earth, and humanity fundamentally share the same…

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
此理但憧憧之徒容心於擾擾而不能行其所
无事故始與天地不相似耳聖人作易无非欲
人克去巳私以求復乎天地之性觀象玩辭觀
變玩占豈容巳其功哉
書
有言逆于汝心必求諸道有言遜于汝志
必求諸非道
丁濬
同考試官教諭李批場中作者類於逆遜與順
===
上漫說而於所謂求諸道求諸非道者多欠體貼惟
此篇辭理俱到至於矯情之偏處尤發明得透徹真
得老臣告君之體錄之以為學書者式
考試官教諭魏批氣昌理明可取
考試官教諭林批寫得伊尹意思出
大臣告君以聽言之要所以矯乎情之偏也夫
以人言之順逆而為巳之從違此情之偏也上
於聽言之際可不審於是哉伊尹告太甲欲其
矯情之偏者如此意謂進言者未必皆合於道
punctuated:
此理，但憧憧之徒容心於擾擾，而不能行其所无事，故始與天地不相似耳。聖人作易，无非欲人克去巳私，以求復乎天地之性。觀象玩辭，觀變玩占，豈容巳其功哉？

書

有言逆于汝心，必求諸道；有言遜于汝志，必求諸非道。

丁濬

同考試官教諭李批：場中作者類於逆遜與順上漫說，而於所謂求諸道、求諸非道者，多欠體貼。惟此篇辭理俱到，至於矯情之偏處，尤發明得透徹，真得老臣告君之體。錄之以為學書者式。

考試官教諭魏批：氣昌理明，可取。

考試官教諭林批：寫得伊尹意思出。

大臣告君以聽言之要，所以矯乎情之偏也。夫以人言之順逆而為巳之從違，此情之偏也。上於聽言之際，可不審於是哉？伊尹告太甲，欲其矯情之偏者如此。意謂進言者未必皆合於道。
translation_en:
…this principle. Yet those whose thoughts rush restlessly to and fro entangle their minds in turmoil and cannot act without needless contrivance; only thus do they cease to resemble Heaven and Earth. The sage composed the Book of Changes solely to have people overcome their selfishness and seek to recover the nature shared with Heaven and Earth. In contemplating the images and pondering the statements, observing the changes and pondering the divinations, how could they allow their efforts to cease?

Book of Documents

“When words run counter to your heart, you must examine whether they accord with the Way; when words comply with your wishes, you must examine whether they depart from the Way.”

Ding Jun

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Most writers in the examination speak loosely about opposition, compliance, and accord [?], but show little close understanding of what is meant by examining whether words accord with the Way or depart from it. This essay alone achieves excellence in both expression and reasoning. Its explanation of correcting partiality in one’s feelings is especially penetrating. It truly captures the manner of a veteran minister admonishing his ruler. It is recorded here as a model for students of the Book of Documents.

Comment by Examiner Wei, Instructor: Its spirit is vigorous and its reasoning clear; it merits selection.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: It brings out Yi Yin’s meaning.

A great minister instructs his ruler in the essentials of listening to advice in order to correct partiality in his feelings. To accept or reject what others say according to whether it pleases or displeases oneself is precisely such partiality. When listening to advice, can a ruler fail to scrutinize this? Such was Yi Yin’s purpose in admonishing Tai Jia: he wished him to correct the partiality of his feelings. His meaning was that those who offer advice do not necessarily all accord with the Way…

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
傳述而已矣若更有所創輙欲相侔於開物之
功豈我所能乎所以然者亦惟信古而好之焉
耳盖古焉弗信或疑之而妄有所作吾則信之
也篤而知其言之不誣信焉弗好又忽之而漫
無所述我則好之也專而味其意之無倦言必
詩書用惟禮樂想像之頃恍若精神之與合雖
欲不傳情能以自已耶心存周易志在春秋孚
契之餘儼乎形容之若見雖欲立異心能以自
安耶吁作固夫子之能事也乃辭之而以述自
===
居其謙已之意至矣抑夫子賢於堯舜者也而
於作焉何有今既不敢當作者之聖而於老彭
之賢亦不敢顯然以自附盖盛德之言有如此
者然集群聖之大成而折衷之其事雖述而功
則倍於作矣噫以此垂訓後世猶有續經擬經
以自僭者何哉
凡事豫則立不豫則廢言前定則不跲事
前定則不困行前定則不疚道前定則不
窮
punctuated:
傳述而已矣。若更有所創，輙欲相侔於開物之功，豈我所能乎？所以然者，亦惟信古而好之焉耳。盖古焉弗信，或疑之而妄有所作，吾則信之也篤，而知其言之不誣；信焉弗好，又忽之而漫無所述，我則好之也專，而味其意之無倦。言必《詩》《書》，用惟禮樂，想像之頃，恍若精神之與合，雖欲不傳，情能以自已耶？心存《周易》，志在《春秋》，孚契之餘，儼乎形容之若見，雖欲立異，心能以自安耶？吁！作固夫子之能事也，乃辭之而以述自居，其謙已之意至矣！抑夫子賢於堯舜者也，而於作焉何有？今既不敢當作者之聖，而於老彭之賢，亦不敢顯然以自附。盖盛德之言有如此者。然集群聖之大成而折衷之，其事雖述，而功則倍於作矣。噫！以此垂訓後世，猶有續經、擬經以自僭者，何哉？

凡事豫則立，不豫則廢。言前定則不跲，事前定則不困，行前定則不疚，道前定則不窮。
translation_en:
…merely transmitting and recounting. Were I to create something further, immediately seeking to rival the achievement of opening people's understanding, how could that lie within my powers? My reason for this is simply that I trust and love antiquity. For if one does not trust antiquity, one may doubt it and rashly create something of one's own. My trust, however, is firm, and I know that its words are not false. If one trusts it without loving it, one may neglect it and carelessly leave it untransmitted. My love, however, is wholehearted, and I savor its meaning without weariness. My words invariably draw upon the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents; my practice employs only ritual and music. As I imagine the ancients, it seems that my spirit joins with theirs. Even if I wished not to transmit their teachings, could my feelings allow me to stop? My mind dwells on the Changes of Zhou, and my aspirations rest in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Through this sympathetic accord, it is as though I could plainly see the ancients' forms and features. Even if I wished to set myself apart, could my heart find peace in doing so?

Ah! Creating was certainly within the Master's powers, yet he disclaimed it and placed himself among transmitters. His intention to humble himself was consummate! Moreover, the Master surpassed Yao and Shun in worthiness: what difficulty could creating have presented to him? Yet he not only dared not claim the sagehood of a creator, but even dared not openly associate himself with the worthiness of Lao Peng. Such are the words of one of abundant virtue. Nevertheless, he brought together the consummate achievements of all the sages and adjudicated among them. Though his undertaking was transmission, his achievement was twice that of creation. Alas! With this teaching handed down to later generations, why are there still those who presumptuously claim such authority by continuing the Classics or composing imitations of them?

In all things, preparation brings success; without preparation, they fail. When words are settled beforehand, one does not stumble in speaking. When affairs are settled beforehand, one does not encounter difficulty. When conduct is settled beforehand, one has no cause for remorse. When the Way is settled beforehand, one does not reach an impasse.

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
知之而顧有失者何哉蓋人主一時之見毎受
欺於其遜志而忘情於其逆己固所難免也抑
孰知諫鼓之設謗木之立聖人且然而况後世
者乎太甲不類嘗不惠阿衡矣尹恐其病未除
而復萌故藥之以此忠愛何如哉
政貴有恒辭尚體要不惟好異
易詔
同考試官教諭李批經生作經義𫝊將旌别淑慝
一句填塞在内反覆纒繞令人厭觀至講好異處便自
===
支離而多與上文不相關涉最為失旨此作認理真切
而詞更純雅形容周家仁厚立國之體宛然在目故録
考試官教諭魏批作冊命文當如此
考試官教諭林批詞簡理完是亦知體要者
賢王於大臣告以為治之體戒其妨治之事蓋
治皆有體而不可易焉者也苟惟異是好焉則
妨乎其治矣豈善於為治者乎康王命畢公保
釐東郊告之及此蓋謂為治者當先識其體公
往東郊其知所務哉是故旌别殷民不能以無
punctuated:
知之而顧有失者，何哉？蓋人主一時之見，毎受欺於其遜志，而忘情於其逆己，固所難免也。抑孰知諫鼓之設、謗木之立，聖人且然，而况後世者乎？太甲不類，嘗不惠阿衡矣。尹恐其病未除而復萌，故藥之以此，忠愛何如哉！

政貴有恒，辭尚體要，不惟好異。

易詔

同考試官教諭李批：經生作經義，𫝊「將旌别淑慝」一句填塞在内，反覆纒繞，令人厭觀；至講好異處，便自支離，而多與上文不相關涉，最為失旨。此作認理真切，而詞更純雅，形容周家仁厚立國之體，宛然在目，故録。

考試官教諭魏批：作冊命文，當如此。

考試官教諭林批：詞簡理完，是亦知體要者。

賢王於大臣，告以為治之體，戒其妨治之事。蓋治皆有體，而不可易焉者也。苟惟異是好焉，則妨乎其治矣，豈善於為治者乎？康王命畢公保釐東郊，告之及此，蓋謂為治者當先識其體。公往東郊，其知所務哉！是故旌别殷民，不能以無
translation_en:
…knowing this, why should he nevertheless err? A ruler’s judgment at a particular moment is often deceived by what accords with his wishes, while he loses his composure at what opposes him; this is indeed difficult to avoid. Yet consider the establishment of drums for remonstrance and wooden posts for criticism: even the sages provided these, so how much more necessary are they for later generations! Tai Jia was unworthy and once failed to heed the A-heng, the chief minister. Yin feared that his illness had not been eradicated and would recur, and therefore administered this admonition as medicine. How great were his loyalty and loving concern!

“In government, constancy is prized; in pronouncements, substance and essentials are esteemed. Do not merely delight in novelty.”

Yi Zhao

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: When examination candidates compose interpretations of the Classics, they cram in the phrase “will distinguish the good from the wicked” [?], endlessly circling around it until the reader tires of looking at it. When they reach the discussion of delighting in novelty, their argument becomes disjointed and largely unrelated to what precedes it, departing most seriously from the intended meaning. This composition grasps the principle accurately and incisively, and its language is moreover pure and elegant. It depicts so vividly the benevolence and generosity upon which the Zhou founded their state that these seem present before our eyes. It has therefore been included.

Examiner Wei, Instructor, comments: A text conveying a formal royal appointment should be written like this.

Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: The language is concise and the reasoning complete. Here is someone who also understands substance and essentials.

A worthy king instructs his great minister in the fundamental principles of government and warns him against practices that obstruct it. For government has fundamental principles that cannot be altered. If one delights only in novelty, one obstructs one’s government; could such a person be skilled in governing? When King Kang commanded the Duke of Bi to safeguard and administer the eastern suburbs, his instructions extended to this matter. His meaning was that those who govern must first understand its fundamental principles. As the duke went to the eastern suburbs, surely he should know where to direct his efforts! Thus, in distinguishing among the people of Yin, one cannot dispense with…

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
政也使不有恒則徒法矣民孰與守汝必惟有
恒之是式循其常而使相安通其變而使不倦
於凡法制之行皆經常不易之道也斯其爲可
貴乎訓化殷民不能以無辭也使失體要則徒
言矣民孰與信汝必惟體要之是存趣完具而
理不浮體會歸而詞不泛於凡播告之脩皆協
于克一之論也斯其爲可尚乎夫然則爲治之
體立矣而其所以妨乎治者可忽之哉誠以政
固貴於有恒而有恒與異每相違也汝若厭其
===
常以爲不樂爲則將作其聰明務有以新人之
耳目悅須臾而爲異常之事矣殊不知暫雖異
也而久必乖如政體何公其戒之無立異以自
高焉辭固尚於體要而體要與異每相反也汝
若惡其同以爲不欲爲則將騁其私智務有以
駭人之見聞喜夸詐而爲異同之辯矣殊不知
文雖異也而理必悖如辭令何公其戒之無求
異以自衒焉吁政有體也而異非所貴辭有體
也而異非所尚康王以是而告公可謂得冊命
punctuated: 政也。使不有恒，則徒法矣，民孰與守？汝必惟有恒之是式，循其常而使相安，通其變而使不倦。於凡法制之行，皆經常不易之道也，斯其爲可貴乎！訓化殷民，不能以無辭也。使失體要，則徒言矣，民孰與信？汝必惟體要之是存，趣完具而理不浮，體會歸而詞不泛。於凡播告之脩，皆協于克一之論也，斯其爲可尚乎！夫然，則爲治之體立矣，而其所以妨乎治者，可忽之哉？誠以政固貴於有恒，而有恒與異每相違也。汝若厭其常，以爲不樂爲，則將作其聰明，務有以新人之耳目，悅須臾而爲異常之事矣。殊不知暫雖異也，而久必乖，如政體何？公其戒之，無立異以自高焉！辭固尚於體要，而體要與異每相反也。汝若惡其同，以爲不欲爲，則將騁其私智，務有以駭人之見聞，喜夸詐而爲異同之辯矣。殊不知文雖異也，而理必悖，如辭令何？公其戒之，無求異以自衒焉！吁！政有體也，而異非所貴；辭有體也，而異非所尚。康王以是而告公，可謂得冊命
translation_en:
…governmental measures. If these lack constancy, they will be mere laws: with whom will the people join in observing them? You must take constancy alone as your model, following established practices so that people live together in peace, and adapting to change so that they do not grow weary. Every implementation of laws and institutions must follow enduring, unchanging principles. Is this not what deserves to be prized? Instructing and transforming the people of Yin cannot be accomplished without words. If these lack substance and essentials, they will be mere talk: with whom will the people join in trusting them? You must preserve substance and essentials alone, making the purport complete and the reasoning substantial, grasping the ultimate import and keeping the wording focused. Every proclamation you prepare must accord with coherent and consistent reasoning. Is this not what deserves to be esteemed?

With this, the proper framework of government is established. But can the things that obstruct good government be disregarded? Government indeed prizes constancy, and constancy and novelty are often at odds. If you tire of established practices and find no pleasure in following them, you will begin displaying your cleverness, striving to present something new to people’s eyes and ears, and undertaking extraordinary measures for a moment’s gratification. You fail to realize that, though these may seem novel for a time, they will inevitably go awry in the long run. What then becomes of the proper framework of government? Duke, be on your guard: do not set yourself apart merely to exalt yourself!

In language, substance and essentials are indeed esteemed, and these are often opposed to novelty. If you dislike conformity and are unwilling to follow it, you will give free rein to your private cleverness, striving to startle people with what they see and hear, delighting in exaggeration and deception, and engaging in disputations over differences and similarities. You fail to realize that, though the wording may be novel, its reasoning will inevitably be perverse. What then becomes of official pronouncements? Duke, be on your guard: do not seek novelty merely to show yourself off!

Ah! Government has its proper form, and novelty is not what it prizes; language has its proper form, and novelty is not what it esteems. In admonishing the Duke in these terms, King Kang may be said to have grasped, in issuing a written investiture command…

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之恒者矣女公□□□□□政績久著於國
為政不患其不恒師言素重於朝命辭不患其
無體要好異之事知其必無也康王乃以是告
之何哉盖當是時商俗未化靡靡之風盛而有
恒之政微利口之習深而體要之辭變在公雖
無是失而所以告戒之道當如是也噫有周君
臣規飭之氣象於此猶可想見
詩
肅肅謝功召伯營之烈烈征師召伯成之
張恦
同考試官教諭吳批以肅肅言邑功以烈烈言
征師此詩人善形容處能體貼成文者莫過此篇
同考試官教諭陳批此皆歸美之詞見召伯感
人之素作文者已得之矣
同考試官學正周批道徒役當時歸美意不啻
若自其口出
考試官教諭魏批此雅詩近風者文亦類之
考試官教諭林批善寫召公克副哲命之意
punctuated:
之恒者矣。女公□□□□□，政績久著於國，為政不患其不恒；師言素重於朝，命辭不患其無體要。好異之事，知其必無也。康王乃以是告之，何哉？盖當是時，商俗未化，靡靡之風盛，而有恒之政微；利口之習深，而體要之辭變。在公雖無是失，而所以告戒之道當如是也。噫！有周君臣規飭之氣象，於此猶可想見。
詩
肅肅謝功，召伯營之；烈烈征師，召伯成之。
張恦
同考試官教諭吳批：以肅肅言邑功，以烈烈言征師，此詩人善形容處。能體貼成文者，莫過此篇。
同考試官教諭陳批：此皆歸美之詞，見召伯感人之素，作文者已得之矣。
同考試官學正周批：道徒役當時歸美意，不啻若自其口出。
考試官教諭魏批：此雅詩近風者，文亦類之。
考試官教諭林批：善寫召公克副哲命之意。
translation_en:
…one who understood the enduring principles of investiture commands. You, Duke, [five illegible characters]: your achievements in government have long been manifest throughout the realm, so there is no fear that your administration will lack constancy. Your words of instruction [?] have long carried weight at court, so there is no fear that your pronouncements will lack substance and concision. We know that you would certainly never indulge a taste for novelty. Why, then, did King Kang admonish you in these terms? At that time, the customs of Shang had not yet been transformed. A languid, decadent ethos prevailed, while constancy in government had declined; glib speaking was deeply ingrained, while substantial and concise expression had become corrupted. Although the duke had no such faults, this was nevertheless the proper way to admonish him. Ah! Here we can still picture the spirit in which the rulers and ministers of Zhou admonished and disciplined one another.
Book of Odes
“Diligent was the work at Xie; the Earl of Shao planned it. Mighty was the host on the march; the Earl of Shao brought its task to completion.”
Zhang Shang 張恦
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor of a county school, comments: “Using ‘diligent’ to describe the work on the city and ‘mighty’ to describe the marching host—this is where the poet excels at description. No essay surpasses this one in grasping these nuances and giving them written expression.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor of a county school, comments: “These are all words attributing praise, revealing the Earl of Shao’s long-established ability to move people. The essay’s author has grasped this.”
Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor of a subprefectural school, comments: “It conveys the laborers’ intention in offering praise at that time just as though the words came from their own mouths.”
Examiner Wei, Instructor of a county school, comments: “This is an ode from the Court Hymns that resembles the Airs of the States; the essay likewise resembles them.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor of a county school, comments: “It skillfully conveys how the Duke of Shao could fully carry out the wise royal command.”

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
詩人於大臣而以其所治□□□□□□□□馬夫
大臣所治者城邑所統者徒□□□□□其賢殆足
以有功詩人亦烏得而歸美之哉宣王封申伯
于謝命召穆公往營城邑故將徒役南行而行
者作此以為封謝者國之大典也而營謝者國
之重務也誠以營度非人則無以壯其國邑體
勢為之不重矣今此謝功宮室門社之鼎建棟
宇簷阿峻起而軒翔也城郭樓櫓之聿新制度
規模整飭而弘壯也是肅肅之功豈他人能營
===
之實我召伯教護屬工凡以程土物而度有司
者皆聽其指揮董課章程凡以定經制而平版
榦者悉資其區畫是其作事雖出於眾工而營
之者非我伯其誰歟若夫統御非人則無以激
勸人心而邑功為之弗亟矣今此征師志氣踴
躍毅然於道途之上而畧其室家之念精神奮
發矯然於畚鍤之餘而忘其歲月之侵是烈烈
之師豈他人能成之實我召公以恤下為德凡
以節其勞而憫其病者自有以感乎人心以集
punctuated: 詩人於大臣而以其所治□□□□□□□□馬。夫大臣所治者城邑，所統者徒□□□□□其賢殆足以有功，詩人亦烏得而歸美之哉？宣王封申伯于謝，命召穆公往營城邑，故將徒役南行，而行者作此，以為封謝者國之大典也，而營謝者國之重務也。誠以營度非人，則無以壯其國邑，體勢為之不重矣。今此謝功，宮室門社之鼎建，棟宇簷阿峻起而軒翔也；城郭樓櫓之聿新，制度規模整飭而弘壯也。是肅肅之功，豈他人能營之？實我召伯教護屬工，凡以程土物而度有司者，皆聽其指揮；董課章程，凡以定經制而平版榦者，悉資其區畫。是其作事雖出於眾工，而營之者非我伯其誰歟？若夫統御非人，則無以激勸人心，而邑功為之弗亟矣。今此征師，志氣踴躍，毅然於道途之上而畧其室家之念；精神奮發，矯然於畚鍤之餘而忘其歲月之侵。是烈烈之師，豈他人能成之？實我召公以恤下為德，凡以節其勞而憫其病者，自有以感乎人心；以集
translation_en:
The poet, speaking of a great minister and what he administered, [eight illegible characters; the following 馬 is doubtful] [?]. Now, what a great minister administers is cities and settlements; those he commands are laborers [five illegible characters]. His worthiness is perhaps sufficient to achieve merit [?]; how, then, could the poet attribute the credit to him?

King Xuan enfeoffed Shen Bo at Xie and ordered Duke Mu of Shao to go there and build the city. He therefore led the laborers southward, and those who went composed this poem. They considered the granting of Xie as a fief a great ceremony of the state, and the building of Xie an important undertaking of the state. Indeed, if planning and construction were entrusted to the wrong person, there would be no means of strengthening the city of that domain, and its configuration and strategic position would lack imposing weight.

Now, in this construction at Xie, palaces and dwellings, gates and altars of the soil have been grandly established; beams, roofs, eaves, and roof corners rise steeply and soar aloft. City walls, outer walls, towers, and watchtowers have been newly built; their design and scale are orderly, expansive, and imposing. Could anyone else have planned this “stately” achievement? It was truly our Earl of Shao who instructed and watched over the assembled craftsmen. All who assessed the earth and materials and apportioned duties to the responsible officers obeyed his directions. He supervised and evaluated their work according to established rules; all who fixed the dimensions and aligned the boards and posts for rammed-earth construction relied upon his arrangements. Thus, although the work was performed by the many craftsmen, who but our earl planned it?

As for command, if it were entrusted to the wrong person, there would be no means of inspiring and encouraging men’s hearts, and the city’s construction would consequently fail to proceed swiftly. Now these men on the expedition are eager in spirit and purpose. Resolute upon the road, they put aside thoughts of their households; vigorous and spirited even after laboring with baskets and spades, they forget the encroachment of the months and years. Could anyone else have formed this “ardent” host? It was truly our Duke of Shao who took solicitude for those below him as his virtue. title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
事爲忠凡以作其勤而警其怠者又有以勵乎
士氣是其敢奮雖在於我輩而成之者非我公
其誰歟夫以召伯之功如是則上慰王者待元
舅之念下成親臣保南土之功而豈細故也哉
詩人可謂善言其功者矣抑考之易觀象於雲
雷而知建侯之道玩占於順險而知帥師之宜
宣王之封建雲雷之義也召伯之營謝其知順
險者乎嗚呼先王之用人以得人心爲本宣王
得召公之心而任之召公得師徒之心而役之
===
其於營謝何有後世犬馬其臣而牛羊其民有
如皇甫之作都者可以深戒也夫
威儀孔時君子有孝子孝子不匱永錫爾
類
李文瑞
同考試官教諭吳批此題與上下章血脉聯絡
可以該括嘏詞祝君之意所謂常山之蛇擊其中而
首尾俱應者也是作獨得之
同考試官教諭陳批意思完具而詞釆不浮經
punctuated:
事爲忠，凡以作其勤而警其怠者，又有以勵乎士氣。是其敢奮雖在於我輩，而成之者非我公，其誰歟？夫以召伯之功如是，則上慰王者待元舅之念，下成親臣保南土之功，而豈細故也哉！詩人可謂善言其功者矣。抑考之《易》，觀象於雲雷而知建侯之道，玩占於順險而知帥師之宜。宣王之封建，雲雷之義也；召伯之營謝，其知順險者乎！嗚呼！先王之用人，以得人心爲本。宣王得召公之心而任之，召公得師徒之心而役之，其於營謝何有？後世犬馬其臣，而牛羊其民，有如皇甫之作都者，可以深戒也夫！
威儀孔時，君子有孝子。孝子不匱，永錫爾類。
李文瑞
同考試官教諭吳批：此題與上下章血脉聯絡，可以該括嘏詞祝君之意。所謂常山之蛇，擊其中而首尾俱應者也。是作獨得之。
同考試官教諭陳批：意思完具，而詞釆不浮。經
translation_en:
…regards accomplishing the work as loyalty. Everything he does to encourage diligence and admonish indolence further heartens the men. Thus, although the courage to exert ourselves lies with us, who but our lord has brought it about? With the Earl of Shao’s achievements such as these, he fulfills, above, the king’s hopes for his senior maternal uncle and, below, accomplishes the task of a kinsman-minister securing the southern lands. How could this be a minor matter! The poet may indeed be said to have expressed his achievements well.
Moreover, examining the Book of Changes, we contemplate the images of clouds and thunder and understand the way to establish feudal lords; we ponder the prognostication concerning compliance and danger and understand the proper way to lead an army. King Xuan’s establishment of a fief embodies the meaning of clouds and thunder. Did not the Earl of Shao’s construction of Xie show his understanding of compliance and danger? Ah! When the former kings employed men, they took winning their hearts as the foundation. King Xuan won the Duke of Shao’s heart and entrusted him with office; the Duke of Shao won the hearts of his troops and put them to work. What difficulty, then, was there in building Xie? In later ages, rulers treated their ministers as dogs and horses and their people as cattle and sheep. Cases such as Huangfu’s construction of a capital should serve as a profound warning!
“Your dignified bearing is most fitting; you, lord, have a filial son. The filial son’s devotion is inexhaustible; blessings will forever be bestowed upon your kind.”
Li Wenrui
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: This topic is intimately connected with the preceding and following stanzas and can encompass the intention of the words of blessing offered to the lord. It is like the proverbial snake of Mount Chang: strike its middle, and head and tail both respond. This composition alone has grasped this.
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: The ideas are complete, and the ornate diction is not frivolous. A classical …

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
生似此亦可與言文矣
同考試官學正周批朱傳宜字能體認講類字
用胤祚意而不露其詞其學詩有得者歟
考試官教諭魏批詩意牽聯不斷而文不失
其意
考試官教諭林批講孔時不匱殊明白
詩人述嘏詞荅君惟祭有以協其誠宜神有以
永其庇夫祭以誠為之本也王者奉祭以至於
舉奠者無不用其誠焉則神豈有不永庇之哉
===
既醉之詩父兄所以荅行葦也及此乃述尸告
之詞若曰追遠者多怠於終獲善者恒難於久
焉知神之意乎盖以今者之祭而其主則吾君
焉但見孝心內蘊形而為對越之容其立也詘
其進也愉而禮儀無不卒度誠意中涵著而為
裸將之敬其親也慤其行也趨而動容無不中
禮威儀何甚時耶迨祭之終而其禮有舉奠焉
吾君之嗣子也孝因於心篤之於廟庭入而受
胙盖已在旅酬之後矣猶必盡其敬而敬定乎
punctuated:
生似此，亦可與言文矣。
同考試官學正周批：朱傳宜字能體認，講類字用胤祚意而不露其詞，其學詩有得者歟？
考試官教諭魏批：詩意牽聯不斷，而文不失其意。
考試官教諭林批：講孔時、不匱殊明白。
詩人述嘏詞荅君，惟祭有以協其誠，宜神有以永其庇。夫祭以誠為之本也，王者奉祭，以至於舉奠者，無不用其誠焉，則神豈有不永庇之哉？
《既醉》之詩，父兄所以荅《行葦》也。及此，乃述尸告之詞，若曰：追遠者多怠於終，獲善者恒難於久，焉知神之意乎？盖以今者之祭，而其主則吾君焉。但見孝心內蘊，形而為對越之容，其立也詘，其進也愉，而禮儀無不卒度；誠意中涵，著而為裸將之敬，其親也慤，其行也趨，而動容無不中禮。威儀何甚時耶！迨祭之終，而其禮有舉奠焉。吾君之嗣子也，孝因於心，篤之於廟庭，入而受胙，盖已在旅酬之後矣，猶必盡其敬，而敬定乎
translation_en:
…A student of the classics such as this is someone with whom one may indeed discuss literary composition.
Associate Examiner Zhou, an Instructor, comments: He has grasped the sense of the word “fitting” in Zhu Xi’s commentary. In explaining “kind,” he employs the idea of posterity and dynastic blessings without explicitly using those terms. Surely he has gained insight from his study of the Book of Odes!
Examiner Wei, an Instructor, comments: The meanings of the ode are linked in an unbroken sequence, and the essay remains faithful to them.
Examiner Lin, an Instructor, comments: His explanations of “most timely” and “never exhausted” are exceptionally clear.
The poet recounts the words of blessing in response to the ruler: since the sacrifice gives fitting expression to his sincerity, it is proper that the spirits should perpetuate their protection. Sincerity is the foundation of sacrifice. When a king performs a sacrifice, even down to the raising of the offered cup, he exercises sincerity in everything. How, then, could the spirits fail to protect him forever?
The ode “Already Drunk” (Ji zui) is the response of the fathers and elder brothers to “The Reeds along the Path” (Xing wei). At this point it recounts the pronouncement of the ancestral impersonator, as though saying: Those who honor their distant ancestors often grow slack toward the end; those who obtain blessings always find it difficult to sustain them. How can one know the spirits’ intent? Now, at the present sacrifice, its presiding host is our ruler. We see only filial devotion stored within him, taking outward form in his demeanor as he faces the spirits: he stands with his body bent and advances with pleasure, and every ritual observance accords fully with the prescribed measures. Sincerity held within manifests itself in the reverence of his libation offering: he approaches with earnestness and moves with quickened steps, and every movement and expression accords with ritual. How perfectly timely is his dignified bearing!
When the sacrifice approaches its end, its rites include the raising of the offered cup. Our ruler’s heir, whose filial devotion is rooted in his heart and earnestly expressed in the ancestral temple courtyard, enters to receive the sacrificial meat. Although this is already after the communal exchange of toasts, he must still exercise his reverence to the utmost, and his reverence remains fixed upon …

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
祝祭之初也孝子之舉奠也誠根於中敦之於
祀事酌而獻尸盖已在告成之際矣猶必盡其
信而信恍乎迎牲之始也孝誠寧有匱耶夫一
祭之間而無所不備如此彼籩豆靜嘉猶曰盡
夫物爾今則見其威儀之甚時是宜隆爾以幽
貺朋友攸攝猶曰相以人爾今則徴其孝誠之
不匱是宜惠爾以無疆默有以相之永錫以元
吉之休有所集斯有所受始之於今日者將衍
於萬年焉陰有以扶之恒畀以貞嘉之慶有所
授斯有所承肇之於一時者將垂於永久焉因
吾君之孝享兾吾君之恒吉此公尸之詞神之
意也亦吾人之深願也噫既醉詩人何其忠愛
之懇至與載觀行葦之遇同姓凡其需於燕者
無所不致其備既行射爲樂復舉酒以爲壽焉
上之恩亦云厚矣親親之仁也則其父兄耆老
感激思報奚容已哉故祝之以神貺而必爲可
大可久之圖於此既曰永錫爾類至下章又反
覆以萬年祚胤爲言正以發此意爾尊尊之義
punctuated: 祝祭之初也。孝子之舉奠也，誠根於中，敦之於祀事，酌而獻尸，盖已在告成之際矣，猶必盡其信，而信恍乎迎牲之始也。孝誠寧有匱耶？夫一祭之間，而無所不備如此，彼籩豆靜嘉，猶曰盡夫物爾；今則見其威儀之甚時，是宜隆爾以幽貺。朋友攸攝，猶曰相以人爾；今則徴其孝誠之不匱，是宜惠爾以無疆。默有以相之，永錫以元吉之休，有所集斯有所受，始之於今日者將衍於萬年焉；陰有以扶之，恒畀以貞嘉之慶，有所授斯有所承，肇之於一時者將垂於永久焉。因吾君之孝享，兾吾君之恒吉，此公尸之詞，神之意也，亦吾人之深願也。噫！《既醉》詩人何其忠愛之懇至與！載觀《行葦》之遇同姓，凡其需於燕者，無所不致其備；既行射爲樂，復舉酒以爲壽焉。上之恩亦云厚矣，親親之仁也。則其父兄耆老感激思報，奚容已哉？故祝之以神貺，而必爲可大可久之圖。於此既曰「永錫爾類」，至下章又反覆以「萬年祚胤」爲言，正以發此意爾。尊尊之義
translation_en:
…the beginning of the sacrificial invocation. When the filial son raises the offering, his sincerity is rooted within and expressed fully in the sacrificial service. When he pours wine and presents it to the ancestral impersonator, the rite has already reached the point of announcing its completion; yet he must still exercise his trustworthiness to the utmost, as though it were still the beginning, when the sacrificial animal was welcomed [?]. How could his filial sincerity ever be exhausted? Within a single sacrifice, everything is thus fully provided. That the bamboo and wooden offering vessels are clean and fine speaks merely of supplying the requisite objects; now, however, we see how perfectly timely his dignified bearing is, and so it is fitting that you be exalted with blessings from the unseen spirits. That friends assist speaks merely of help supplied by people; now, however, we have proof that his filial sincerity is inexhaustible, and so it is fitting that you receive favor without limit. Silently the spirits assist him, forever bestowing the blessing of supreme good fortune. Where blessings gather, there is someone to receive them; what begins today will extend through ten thousand years. Unseen they support him, continually granting auspicious blessings of steadfast goodness. Where something is bestowed, there is someone to inherit it; what originates at a single moment will endure forever. In response to our lord’s filial offerings, they wish for his lasting good fortune: these are the words of the princely ancestral impersonator and the intention of the spirits, and they are also our own profound wish. Ah! How earnest and deep is the loyal affection of the poet of “Already Drunk” (Jizui)!

Consider also the treatment of those of the same surname in “The Wayside Reeds” (Xingwei): everything needed for their banquet is fully supplied. After archery has provided enjoyment, cups are raised again to wish longevity. The favor shown by the ruler is indeed generous: this is the benevolence of cherishing one’s kin. How, then, could his senior kinsmen and elders restrain their gratitude and their desire to repay him? Thus they invoke spiritual blessings upon him and necessarily devise plans capable of both greatness and endurance. Here the poet has already said, “May blessings forever be bestowed upon your kind”; in the following stanza he returns repeatedly to “For ten thousand years, may your descendants be blessed,” precisely to express this intention. The righteousness of honoring those entitled to honor…

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
也上以是施之下以是報之彼我之間畧無扞
格焉者吾於是益徵有周之泰
春秋
取汶陽田成公二年晉侯使韓穿來言
汶陽之田歸之于齊成公八年公會晉
侯齊侯宋公衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒子杞伯同
盟于蒲成公九年會于蕭魚襄公十一
年楚子蔡侯陳侯鄭伯許男徐子滕子
頓子胡子沈子小邾子宋世子佐淮夷會
===
于申昭公四年
吳允祥
同考試官訓導鄭批每見讀春秋者僅以記傳
為優不思義理深粹往往以易忽之此作發明景悼
之事迥異於衆似有獨得之妙者
同考試官教諭林批詳據盟會而本末得失自
別作者率多引用繁瑣論斷支離使經傳為之一晦
獨此篇說出誠信為服人之本句句不誣是嘗究心
於理者錄之可式
punctuated:
也。上以是施之，下以是報之，彼我之間畧無扞格焉者，吾於是益徵有周之泰。

春秋

取汶陽田，成公二年。晉侯使韓穿來言，汶陽之田歸之于齊，成公八年。公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、杞伯，同盟于蒲，成公九年。會于蕭魚，襄公十一年。楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、鄭伯、許男、徐子、滕子、頓子、胡子、沈子、小邾子、宋世子佐、淮夷會于申，昭公四年。

吳允祥

同考試官訓導鄭批：每見讀《春秋》者，僅以記傳為優，不思義理深粹，往往以易忽之。此作發明景悼之事，迥異於衆，似有獨得之妙者。

同考試官教諭林批：詳據盟會，而本末得失自別。作者率多引用繁瑣，論斷支離，使經傳為之一晦。獨此篇說出誠信為服人之本，句句不誣，是嘗究心於理者，錄之可式。
translation_en:
… Such is the duty of honoring the honored. Those above bestow on this basis, and those below repay on this basis. That there is not the slightest discord between them gives me further evidence of the harmony of the Zhou.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“[Lu] took the fields of Wenyang.” Second year of Duke Cheng.
“The Marquis of Jin sent Han Chuan to come and say that the fields of Wenyang should be returned to Qi.” Eighth year of Duke Cheng.
“The Duke met with the marquises of Jin, Qi, Song, and Wei, the earls of Zheng and Cao, the Viscount of Ju, and the Earl of Qi; they jointly covenanted at Pu.” Ninth year of Duke Cheng.
“They met at Xiaoyu.” Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.
“The Viscount of Chu, the marquises of Cai and Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the viscounts of Xu, Teng, Dun, Hu, Shen, and Xiao Zhu, Zuo, heir apparent of Song, and the Huai Yi met at Shen.” Fourth year of Duke Zhao.

Wu Yunxiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor: I often find that readers of the Spring and Autumn Annals regard mere memorization of its commentaries as an accomplishment. They do not ponder the depth and refinement of its moral principles, and often slight it as easy. This essay elucidates the affairs of Dukes Jing and Dao in a manner quite different from the rest, seemingly displaying the subtlety of an insight independently attained.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Drawing in detail on the covenants and assemblies, the essay clearly distinguishes their beginnings and outcomes, successes and failures. Writers generally pile up cumbersome citations and offer disjointed judgments, thereby obscuring the classic and its commentaries. This essay alone brings out sincerity and trustworthiness as the foundation for winning people’s allegiance. Every sentence is sound: its author has devoted thought to moral principle. Selected for inclusion, it can serve as a model.

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭魏批〔正是謹嚴家數〕
考試官教諭林批〔能以義理為斷案可錄〕
失服人之本而徒以强其從者春秋罪之得服
人之本而是以堅其從者春秋嘉之盖人心向
背顧伯者之誠信何如耳此景悼之本末得失
所以分也慨晋諸侯以汶陽之故而咸有貳心
晋景為盟于蒲以要之自將以為得救其失寧
無以服人乎殊不知信貴在於言前誠貴出於
令外固結之本所當務也奈何景公有昧於此
===
初嘗下令而歸地於魯尋有二命而返地於齊
一予一奪而信不可知諸侯解體殆有由焉景
乃不知惇信明義以補反覆之愆徒欲刑牲歃
血以挽渙散之勢回視馬陵甫踰無幾蹟其要
言詔神勉强相從特亦彼此徒勞焉耳噫盟之
不能强於人如此否則諸侯當自恊矣何以不
能尋夫二年以前之故轍耶春秋特書盟蒲於
歸田之後而罪之者所以為務末而不知本者
之戒迨夫鄭伯以三駕之伐而遂令行成晋悼
punctuated:
考試官教諭魏批〔正是謹嚴家數〕

考試官教諭林批〔能以義理為斷案，可錄〕

失服人之本，而徒以强其從者，《春秋》罪之；得服人之本，而是以堅其從者，《春秋》嘉之。盖人心向背，顧伯者之誠信何如耳。此景悼之本末得失所以分也。慨晋諸侯以汶陽之故而咸有貳心，晋景為盟于蒲以要之，自將以為得救其失，寧無以服人乎？殊不知信貴在於言前，誠貴出於令外，固結之本所當務也。奈何景公有昧於此，初嘗下令而歸地於魯，尋有二命而返地於齊，一予一奪而信不可知，諸侯解體殆有由焉。景乃不知惇信明義，以補反覆之愆，徒欲刑牲歃血，以挽渙散之勢。回視馬陵，甫踰無幾，蹟其要言詔神，勉强相從，特亦彼此徒勞焉耳。噫！盟之不能强於人如此。否則，諸侯當自恊矣，何以不能尋夫二年以前之故轍耶？《春秋》特書盟蒲於歸田之後而罪之者，所以為務末而不知本者之戒。迨夫鄭伯以三駕之伐而遂令行成，晋悼
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wei, Instructor: 〔Precisely the rigorous and disciplined approach.〕

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔Able to make moral principles the basis of judgment; worthy of inclusion.〕

Those who lose the foundation for winning people’s allegiance and merely compel their compliance are condemned by the Spring and Autumn Annals; those who secure that foundation and thereby strengthen their allegiance are commended by it. Whether people’s hearts turn toward or away from a hegemon depends simply on the quality of his sincerity and trustworthiness. This is what distinguishes Dukes Jing and Dao in their attention to fundamentals and secondary matters, and in their successes and failures.

Lamenting that the feudal lords associated with Jin had all become disaffected over the affair of Wenyang, Duke Jing of Jin held a covenant meeting at Pu to bind them. He apparently thought [?] that he had thereby remedied his error: surely he now had a means of winning their allegiance? Little did he understand that trustworthiness must precede one’s words, and sincerity must extend beyond one’s commands. These are the foundations for firmly binding people together, and it is to these that one must attend. Yet Duke Jing was blind to this. First he issued an order returning the territory to Lu; shortly afterward, a second command returned it to Qi. Giving it and then taking it away made his trustworthiness impossible to discern. There was surely a reason why the feudal lords fell away from him.

Jing did not understand that he should uphold trustworthiness and make righteousness manifest to repair the fault of his reversals. He merely sought, by slaughtering a sacrificial animal and smearing its blood on the lips, to reverse the growing disunity. Looking back, scarcely any time had elapsed since the meeting at Maling. Examining how they pledged their words and called upon the spirits, only reluctantly complying with one another, one sees that it was merely wasted effort on both sides. Alas! Such is the inability of covenants to compel people. Otherwise, the feudal lords should have come into accord of themselves. Why, then, could they not follow the course established two years earlier? By expressly recording the covenant at Pu after the return of the lands and thereby condemning it, the Spring and Autumn Annals offers a warning to those who pursue secondary matters without understanding the fundamentals.

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
□會蕭魚以欵之衆將以爲威不克愛安足以
服人乎殊不知信可不言而喻誠可不令而行
固結之本所當急也幸而悼公有見於此納𡊮
禁侵而不疑禮囚歸國而相與一感一應而信
以交孚鄭人懷德無容已焉是以兵不必血非
惟有以革其面牲不待歃自能有以固其心迨
會于申動經踰世顧其執臣辱國撻伐相尋尚
亦始終斯念焉耳噫誠之足以感於人如此否
則鄭國即自叛矣何其有待於二十四年而改
轍耶春秋特書蕭魚於會申之前而嘉之者所
以爲務本而不事末者之勸是知盟誓者要人
之末誠信者服人之本經斯世者可不知所擇
哉雖然悼之有賢於景固云然矣然而還師之
策罃實無負於悼請田之使穿亦有愧於景也
詩曰其惟哲人告之話言罃則得之又曰猶之
不遠是用大諫穿則失之二公行事之臧否寧
不由於用人之得失耶故說者謂爲政以人才
爲先善治者盍於此求之
punctuated: □會蕭魚以欵之，衆將以爲威不克愛，安足以服人乎？殊不知信可不言而喻，誠可不令而行，固結之本所當急也。幸而悼公有見於此，納𡊮禁侵而不疑，禮囚歸國而相與，一感一應，而信以交孚，鄭人懷德無容已焉。是以兵不必血，非惟有以革其面；牲不待歃，自能有以固其心。迨會于申，動經踰世，顧其執臣辱國，撻伐相尋，尚亦始終斯念焉耳。噫！誠之足以感於人如此，否則鄭國即自叛矣，何其有待於二十四年而改轍耶？春秋特書蕭魚於會申之前而嘉之者，所以爲務本而不事末者之勸。是知盟誓者，要人之末；誠信者，服人之本。經斯世者，可不知所擇哉？雖然，悼之有賢於景，固云然矣。然而還師之策，罃實無負於悼；請田之使，穿亦有愧於景也。詩曰：「其惟哲人，告之話言。」罃則得之。又曰：「猶之不遠，是用大諫。」穿則失之。二公行事之臧否，寧不由於用人之得失耶？故說者謂爲政以人才爲先，善治者盍於此求之？
translation_en:
…[illegible] met at Xiaoyu to treat them with sincerity. People would suppose that, if stern authority did not prevail over benevolence, how could one secure others’ submission? They failed to understand that trustworthiness can make itself understood without words, and sincerity can take effect without commands: the foundation for securing firm allegiance is what deserves urgent attention. Fortunately, Duke Dao perceived this. He “received Yuan” [?] and prohibited incursions without suspicion; he treated the captives courteously and sent them home, fostering fellowship. As one side moved the other and the other responded, mutual trust took hold, and the people of Zheng could not help cherishing his virtue. Thus, weapons did not have to be bloodied to achieve more than an outward change of allegiance; without anyone having to smear his lips with a sacrificial victim’s blood, he could himself secure their heartfelt loyalty. By the meeting at Shen, more than a generation had elapsed. Despite the seizure of their ministers, the humiliation of their state, and successive punitive attacks, they still maintained this same disposition throughout.

Ah! Such is sincerity’s power to move people. Otherwise, Zheng would have rebelled at once. Why would it have waited twenty-four years before changing course? The Spring and Autumn Annals specifically records Xiaoyu before the meeting at Shen and commends it, thereby encouraging those who attend to fundamentals rather than pursuing incidentals. We thus know that covenants and oaths are merely incidental means of binding others, while sincerity and trustworthiness are the foundation for winning their submission. Can those who order this world fail to know which to choose?

Nevertheless, although Duke Dao was indeed more worthy than Duke Jing, Ying’s plan to withdraw the army truly did not fail Duke Dao, whereas Chuan’s mission to request the lands gave him cause for shame before Duke Jing. The Book of Odes says: “It is the wise man who is told sound counsel.” Ying fulfilled this principle. It also says: “Your plans do not reach far; therefore I offer this earnest remonstrance.” Chuan failed in this respect. Did not the merits and faults of the two dukes’ actions arise from their successes and failures in employing men? Thus commentators say that, in government, men of talent come first. Should not those who would govern well seek their lesson here?

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
齊人取讙及闡齊人歸讙及闡俱哀公
八年
王德純
同考試官訓導鄭批拈書得此亦可為易矣作
者於言魯處頗欠體認何哉子能發之而筆勢雄偉
如此其真為春秋者乎
同考試官教諭林批題本平易而難於作文用
傳語則陳言援之舍之又不可也出新奇於陳腐如此
者甚少錄之可以式矣
===
考試官教諭魏批健而不倔春秋義當如此
考試官教諭林批斷魯之善惡詞簡而嚴
春秋於地之得失有著外逆而原其惡於內者
有著外順而顯其善於內者此齊之逆順皆魯
有以自取之也何則讙闡者魯故地也齊曷為
而取之盖邾益齊出也我哀恃強凌弱入而執
之齊人寧不為之動念乎於是取我二邑請吳
三軍而怒猶未怠焉孰不以齊暴也而不知曰
伐曰入誰為之先孰不以齊貪也而不知以獻
punctuated:
齊人取讙及闡，齊人歸讙及闡。俱哀公八年。
王德純。
同考試官訓導鄭批：拈書得此，亦可為易矣。作者於言魯處頗欠體認，何哉？子能發之，而筆勢雄偉如此，其真為春秋者乎！
同考試官教諭林批：題本平易，而難於作文。用傳語則陳言，援之舍之，又不可也。出新奇於陳腐如此者甚少，錄之可以式矣。
考試官教諭魏批：健而不倔，春秋義當如此。
考試官教諭林批：斷魯之善惡，詞簡而嚴。
春秋於地之得失，有著外逆而原其惡於內者，有著外順而顯其善於內者。此齊之逆順，皆魯有以自取之也。何則？讙闡者，魯故地也。齊曷為而取之？盖邾益，齊出也。我哀恃強凌弱，入而執之，齊人寧不為之動念乎？於是取我二邑，請吳三軍，而怒猶未怠焉。孰不以齊暴也，而不知曰伐曰入，誰為之先？孰不以齊貪也，而不知以獻
translation_en:
“The men of Qi seized Huan and Chan”; “The men of Qi returned Huan and Chan.” Both entries are from the eighth year of Duke Ai.
By Wang Dechun.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Assistant Instructor: “To draw this passage from the book as a topic might be considered easy. The author is rather deficient in understanding where he discusses Lu—why is this? Yet you can elucidate it with such a powerful sweep of the brush: are you truly a practitioner of Spring and Autumn Annals interpretation?”
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The topic itself is straightforward, but composing an essay on it is difficult. Using the Commentary’s language produces hackneyed phrasing; yet neither borrowing it nor abandoning it will quite do. Very few produce something so fresh and striking from stale material. This deserves to be recorded as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Wei, Instructor: “Vigorous without being obstinate: an exposition of the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals should be like this.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “In judging Lu’s good and evil, the wording is concise and stern.”
In recording the acquisition and loss of territory, the Spring and Autumn Annals sometimes makes manifest the wrongful conduct of an outside state while tracing the source of its wrongdoing to the home state; sometimes it makes manifest the compliant conduct of an outside state while revealing the goodness within the home state. In this case, Qi’s wrongful and compliant conduct alike were brought upon Lu by its own actions. Why is this? Huan and Chan were Lu’s old territories. Why did Qi seize them? Yi, the ruler of Zhu, was born of a woman of Qi. Our Duke Ai relied on his strength to oppress the weak, invaded Zhu, and took Yi captive. How could the men of Qi fail to be stirred on his behalf? Thereupon they seized our two towns and requested Wu’s three armies, yet their anger still did not abate. Who would not consider Qi violent? title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
因誰遺之感固齊之惡實魯之惡也否則齊
胡為是哉齊有取地之罪魯有失地之辱傳曰
出爾反爾哀實以之聖人惡結怨特書取著齊
之逆而魯君造惡不悛則有謀取其國家莫能
保者讙闡齊既取矣又曷為而歸之盖邿益魯
俘也我哀悔過遷善釋而返之齊怒寧不為之
少怠乎於是侵疆歸我佳兵辭吳而德猶未泯
焉人徒知齊之不暴也而不知我有執邿之悔
以動之人徒知齊之不貪也而不知我有歸邿
===
之事以來之固齊之善實魯之善也否則齊肯
為此哉齊無取地之罪魯無失地之辱語曰過
而不改公何有焉聖人大改過特書歸著齊之
順而魯君去惡不積則有不侵其封境而自安
者吁因其惡而惡之則人不敢於為惡因其善
而善之則人不憚於為善聖人道大德宏樂與
人為善如此其真能司賞罰之權哉大抵天下
莫大於理而理即善也強眾不與焉以魯事觀
之可見矣謂理不足以服人而區區較威力以
punctuated: 因誰遺之感？固齊之惡，實魯之惡也。否則，齊胡為是哉？齊有取地之罪，魯有失地之辱。傳曰：「出爾反爾。」哀實以之。聖人惡結怨，特書「取」，著齊之逆；而魯君造惡不悛，則有謀取其國家莫能保者。讙闡，齊既取矣，又曷為而歸之？盖邿益，魯俘也。我哀悔過遷善，釋而返之，齊怒寧不為之少怠乎？於是侵疆歸我，佳兵辭吳，而德猶未泯焉。人徒知齊之不暴也，而不知我有執邿之悔以動之；人徒知齊之不貪也，而不知我有歸邿之事以來之。固齊之善，實魯之善也。否則，齊肯為此哉？齊無取地之罪，魯無失地之辱。語曰：「過而不改。」公何有焉？聖人大改過，特書「歸」，著齊之順；而魯君去惡不積，則有不侵其封境而自安者。吁！因其惡而惡之，則人不敢於為惡；因其善而善之，則人不憚於為善。聖人道大德宏，樂與人為善如此，其真能司賞罰之權哉！大抵天下莫大於理，而理即善也，強眾不與焉。以魯事觀之，可見矣。謂理不足以服人，而區區較威力以
translation_en:
…who occasioned the feeling that prompted the offering [?]? Though this was Qi’s wrongdoing, it was in truth Lu’s wrongdoing. Otherwise, why would Qi have acted thus? Qi bore the guilt of seizing territory; Lu suffered the disgrace of losing it. The Commentary says, “What goes out from you returns to you.” This indeed applied to Duke Ai. The Sage abhorred the creation of enmity and specifically wrote “seized,” exposing Qi’s defiance. Yet when the ruler of Lu committed wrongs without repenting, there were those who plotted to seize his state, and he could not preserve it.

Once Qi had seized Huan and Chan, why did it return them? Yi of Shi [?] was Lu’s captive. Our Duke Ai repented of his fault and turned toward goodness, releasing him and sending him back. Could Qi’s anger fail to subside somewhat as a result? Thus the occupied borderlands were returned to us, and Wu’s armed forces were dismissed; goodwill had not yet died out. People know only that Qi was not violent; they do not know that our regret over imprisoning the ruler of Shi [?] moved it. People know only that Qi was not greedy; they do not know that our act of returning the ruler of Shi [?] brought this about. Though this was Qi’s goodness, it was in truth Lu’s goodness. Otherwise, would Qi have been willing to do this? Qi was free of the guilt of seizing territory, and Lu was free of the disgrace of losing it. The Analects speaks of “making a mistake and not correcting it.” How could this apply to the duke? The Sage esteemed the correction of faults and specifically wrote “returned,” revealing Qi’s compliance. When the ruler of Lu cast off wrongdoing rather than allowing it to accumulate, others refrained from invading his borders, and he enjoyed security.

Ah! If people are condemned for their wrongdoing, they will not dare to do wrong; if they are commended for their goodness, they will not shrink from doing good. So great is the Sage’s Way, so vast his virtue, and such is his delight in helping others do good! Does he not truly wield the authority of reward and punishment? Generally speaking, nothing under Heaven is greater than principle, and principle is goodness itself. Strength and numbers cannot rival it. This is evident from the affairs of Lu. To say that principle is insufficient to win people’s submission, and instead narrowly to compete in might so as to…

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其必勝之功者何其謬耶然斯時也有孔子焉
苟用之則妙過化存神之功魯可東周矣惜乎
其不能也適越之辱咎將誰執
禮記
樂至則無怨禮至則不爭
梅賢
同考試官訓導李批學者多於無怨不爭處用
下文入講失之繁瑣其不然者則又簡淡而無味此作
能脫去陳腐且詞氣和平蓋嘗有志於禮樂者
===
考試官教諭魏批辭理精到可嘉
考試官教諭林批樂記題必如此講乃得
大樂有以和天下大禮有以序天下夫莫難化
者天下之心也禮樂至而能有以和之序之尚
安有怨爭者哉樂記君子之言如此蓋謂天下
有難一之心君子有能一之道是故欣喜歡愛
之和出於中而靜焉者固為樂而非樂之至也
樂而曰至必其上下同流合絪縕之妙顯微充
塞契摩蕩之機如乾以易知而不勞也是樂可
punctuated:
其必勝之功者，何其謬耶！然斯時也，有孔子焉，苟用之，則妙過化存神之功，魯可東周矣。惜乎其不能也！適越之辱，咎將誰執？
禮記
樂至則無怨，禮至則不爭。
梅賢
同考試官訓導李批：學者多於無怨不爭處，用下文入講，失之繁瑣。其不然者，則又簡淡而無味。此作能脫去陳腐，且詞氣和平，蓋嘗有志於禮樂者。
考試官教諭魏批：辭理精到，可嘉。
考試官教諭林批：樂記題必如此講乃得。
大樂有以和天下，大禮有以序天下。夫莫難化者，天下之心也。禮樂至而能有以和之、序之，尚安有怨爭者哉？樂記君子之言如此，蓋謂天下有難一之心，君子有能一之道。是故欣喜歡愛之和，出於中而靜焉者，固為樂，而非樂之至也。樂而曰至，必其上下同流，合絪縕之妙；顯微充塞，契摩蕩之機。如乾以易知而不勞也，是樂可
translation_en:
…their achievement of certain victory—how mistaken they are! Yet at that time there was Confucius. Had he been employed, he could have wondrously achieved the sage’s work of transforming wherever he passed and exerting spiritual influence wherever he remained, and Lu could have become an Eastern Zhou. Alas, this could not be accomplished! Who, then, should bear the blame for the humiliation of going to Yue?
Record of Rites
“When music reaches its perfection, there is no resentment; when ritual reaches its perfection, there is no contention.”
Mei Xian
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: Most students, when expounding “no resentment” and “no contention,” draw the subsequent text into their discussion and fall into excessive complication. Those who do not, however, are often spare, bland, and without savor. This composition escapes stale conventions, and its language and tone are harmonious and even. Its author must have devoted himself to ritual and music.
Comment by Examiner Wei, Instructor: Both expression and reasoning are refined and exact—commendable.
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: A topic from the Record of Music must be expounded in this way to be properly understood.
Great music provides the means to harmonize all under Heaven; great ritual provides the means to bring order to all under Heaven. Nothing is harder to transform than the hearts of the people throughout the world. If ritual and music reach perfection and can thereby harmonize and order those hearts, how could resentment or contention still exist? Such are the words of the gentleman in the Record of Music. Their meaning is that although the hearts of people throughout the world are difficult to unite, the gentleman possesses a Way capable of uniting them. Thus, the harmony of delight, joy, affection, and love, arising within and finding repose there, is indeed music, but it is not music at its perfection. For music to be called perfect, it must flow alike above and below, accord with the wondrous intermingling of cosmic forces, fill both the manifest and the hidden, and tally with the workings of their mutual interaction and agitation. It is like Qian, the Creative, which presides through ease and without toil. Such music may be called…

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
謂至矣樂之至則自有以和天下之不和而人
皆得其所吾見强不脅弱眾不暴寡欣然同樂
於煕皡之天知不詐愚勇不苦怯怡然相忘於
仁壽之域欲心平而躁心釋蓋無處而非樂化
之流行焉求一人之怨何有乎若夫進退周旋
之序著於外而文焉者固為禮而非禮之至也
禮而曰至必其儀文秩然高下之勢别等威截
然散殊之義明如坤以簡能而不煩也是禮可
謂至矣禮之至則自有以序天下之不序而人
===
各安其分吾見君臣以定貴賤以位凛乎名分
之不敢踰親疎有序長幼有倫肅乎彜常之不
敢亂乖氣息而忿氣消蓋無地而非禮教之通
達焉求一人之爭奚有乎吁禮樂之功效其大
如此茲非所謂至樂無聲而天下和至禮不讓
而天下治者歟雖然禮樂豈易作哉亦豈易言
哉蓋必明於天地之道兼夫德位之隆而後可
以議此是以王者功成作樂治定制禮故能大
有以化乎人心微有以育乎萬物上有以贊乎
punctuated: 謂至矣。樂之至，則自有以和天下之不和，而人皆得其所。吾見强不脅弱，眾不暴寡，欣然同樂於煕皡之天；知不詐愚，勇不苦怯，怡然相忘於仁壽之域。欲心平而躁心釋，蓋無處而非樂化之流行焉，求一人之怨，何有乎？若夫進退周旋之序，著於外而文焉者，固為禮，而非禮之至也。禮而曰至，必其儀文秩然，高下之勢别；等威截然，散殊之義明，如坤以簡能而不煩也。是禮可謂至矣。禮之至，則自有以序天下之不序，而人各安其分。吾見君臣以定，貴賤以位，凛乎名分之不敢踰；親疎有序，長幼有倫，肅乎彜常之不敢亂。乖氣息而忿氣消，蓋無地而非禮教之通達焉，求一人之爭，奚有乎？吁！禮樂之功效，其大如此，茲非所謂至樂無聲而天下和，至禮不讓而天下治者歟？雖然，禮樂豈易作哉？亦豈易言哉？蓋必明於天地之道，兼夫德位之隆，而後可以議此。是以王者功成作樂，治定制禮，故能大有以化乎人心，微有以育乎萬物，上有以贊乎
translation_en:
…may be called consummate. When music reaches perfection, it naturally has the means to harmonize all discord under Heaven, and everyone finds their proper place. I see the strong no longer intimidating the weak, nor the many oppressing the few, all joyfully sharing in music beneath a radiant, tranquil sky; the clever no longer deceiving the foolish, nor the brave tormenting the timid, all contentedly forgetting distinctions between themselves in a realm of benevolence and longevity. Desires are calmed and agitation released. Nowhere does music’s transforming influence fail to flow. Where could one find even a single person harboring resentment?

As for the ordered movements of advancing, withdrawing, turning, and circulating, manifested outwardly in patterned form, these certainly constitute ritual, but not ritual at its perfection. For ritual to be called consummate, its ceremonial forms must be orderly, distinguishing higher and lower positions; its gradations of dignity must be sharply defined, making clear the meaning of differentiated ranks—just as Kun, the Receptive, accomplishes through simplicity without complication. Such ritual may be called consummate. When ritual reaches perfection, it naturally has the means to order all disorder under Heaven, and everyone rests content in their allotted station. I see the positions of ruler and minister established, the noble and lowly assigned their places, all standing in awe of the distinctions of status they dare not overstep; degrees of kinship ordered, elders and juniors properly related, all reverently observing the enduring norms they dare not disrupt. Discordant impulses subside and anger dissipates. Nowhere does ritual instruction fail to penetrate. Where could one find even a single person engaging in contention?

Ah! So great are the achievements of ritual and music! Is this not what is meant by saying that consummate music has no sound, yet all under Heaven is harmonious, and consummate ritual requires no yielding of precedence, yet all under Heaven is well governed? Even so, can ritual and music be easily created? Can they even be easily discussed? Only one who understands the Way of Heaven and Earth and combines exalted virtue with exalted position may deliberate on these matters. Thus, the true king creates music when his achievements are complete and institutes ritual when governance is settled. Hence, on the broad scale, they can transform human hearts; in subtle ways, they can nurture the myriad things; above, they can assist…

title: 正德十一年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
天地幽有以通乎鬼神而成天下之大治馬後
世之君不此之務而淫其樂慝其禮者多矣無
怪乎其民之怨而爭也噫
言而履之禮也行而樂之樂也君子力此
二者以南面而立夫是以天下大平也
呂應陽
同考試官訓導李批言行即禮樂此聖人論禮
樂最親切處謂以此力行以此治人皆非有假於外
也獨此卷以言行二字貫講終篇深得聖人立言之意
===
考試官教諭魏批能說出君子以禮樂致治
之效最為明白非獨工於文而已
考試官教諭林批通篇體貼親切殊快人意
禮樂之得名也切於人禮樂之能行也臻於治
甚矣禮樂之切於人也君子能行之其成天下
之治何有哉夫子告子張為政之道因其復問
而答之及此意謂汝聞為政之在明於禮樂也
孰知禮樂之不外於吾身乎彼人不能無言發
之為難言而履之有以措諸躬行之實而得□
punctuated:
天地，幽有以通乎鬼神，而成天下之大治馬。後世之君不此之務，而淫其樂、慝其禮者多矣，無怪乎其民之怨而爭也。噫！
「言而履之，禮也；行而樂之，樂也。君子力此二者，以南面而立，夫是以天下大平也。」
呂應陽
同考試官訓導李批：言行即禮樂，此聖人論禮樂最親切處。謂以此力行，以此治人，皆非有假於外也。獨此卷以言行二字貫講終篇，深得聖人立言之意。
考試官教諭魏批：能說出君子以禮樂致治之效，最為明白，非獨工於文而已。
考試官教諭林批：通篇體貼親切，殊快人意。
禮樂之得名也，切於人；禮樂之能行也，臻於治。甚矣，禮樂之切於人也！君子能行之，其成天下之治何有哉？夫子告子張為政之道，因其復問而答之及此。意謂：汝聞為政之在明於禮樂也，孰知禮樂之不外於吾身乎？彼人不能無言，發之為難。言而履之，有以措諸躬行之實，而得□
translation_en:
…Heaven and Earth, and, in the unseen realm, communicate with ghosts and spirits, thus bringing about great order throughout the world [?]. Many rulers of later ages have failed to devote themselves to this, instead making their music licentious and their rites corrupt. No wonder their people harbor resentment and contend with one another. Alas!
“To speak and then fulfill one's words is ritual; to act and take delight in doing so is music. The gentleman devotes his strength to these two things and stands facing south as ruler; thereby all under Heaven enjoys great peace.”
Lü Yingyang.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: Words and conduct are themselves ritual and music: this is the most directly pertinent point in the Sage's discussion of ritual and music. He means that one uses these to exert oneself in practice and to govern others, without borrowing anything from outside oneself. This paper alone carries its exposition through from beginning to end with the two terms ‘words’ and ‘conduct,’ profoundly grasping the Sage's intent in making this statement.
Comment by Examiner Wei, Instructor: It explains with exceptional clarity how the gentleman achieves good government through ritual and music. Its merit is more than merely literary skill.
